body:
Split from #1295 (closed as superseded).

## The trap

The /settings sheet reads and writes the global profile only (internal/tui3/settings.go:57-60); the gate resolves through the project ladder (cmd/codeaf/chatv3.go:1590 through config.ProjectStringAt; internal/config/projectconfig.go:269-286), where a .codeaf/config.json answering tools.approvalMode wins wholesale. Inside such a workspace, a sheet edit lands, the live rebuild succeeds (it re-read the project's answer), the receipt says nothing, and the gate is unchanged.

The YOLO badge reads the profile (internal/tui3/app.go:8999), so the badge and the gate can then contradict in both directions: a badge over a gate that asks, or no badge over a gate that runs everything. The code's own false-safety comments (#322, #325) warn about exactly this and nothing on the row, badge, or card names the layer in force.

Adjacent traps to surface on the same rows: a card's "always" cannot apply inside a project-answering repo and the receipt does not say so; --yolo is the one posture a mid-session row edit cannot close (chatv3.go:1594-1596); the free unasked git status ends the moment the first shell rule is written, even a deny (internal/approval, liftsReadOnly requires an empty pattern list).

## The fix direction (approved in #1295)

Every row shows the effective value, with a "set by project" pin when the project layer answers it (a PinnedBy mechanism already exists for other rows). The badge reads the layer the gate reads. Receipts say which layer answered. The shell rules row warns that writing the first rule ends the free git status.

Evidence: audit-notes/permission-wiring.md, sections 3 through 8, every claim at a file:line.

—
